t: For carrying out titles V and XIX of the Public Health Service Act (“PHS Act”) with respect to substance abuse and mental health services, the Protection and Advocacy for Individuals with Mental Illness Act, and section 301 of the PHS Act with respect to program management, $3,237,813,000: Provided, That notwithstanding section 520A(f)(2) of the PHS Act, no funds appropriated for carrying out section 520A are available for carrying out section 1971 of the PHS Act:  Provided further, That in addition to amounts provided herein, the following amounts shall be available under section 241 of the PHS Act: (1) $79,200,000 to carry out subpart II of part B of title XIX of the PHS Act to fund section 1935(b) technical assistance, national data, data collection and evaluation activities, and further that the total available under this Act for section 1935(b) activities shall not exceed 5 percent of the amounts appropriated for subpart II of part B of title XIX; (2) $21,803,000 to carry out subpart I of part B of title XIX of the PHS Act to fund section 1920(b) technical assistance, national data, data collection and evaluation activities, and further that the total available under this Act for section 1920(b) activities shall not exceed 5 percent of the amounts appropriated for subpart I of part B of title XIX; (3) $16,000,000 to carry out national surveys on drug abuse; and (4) $4,300,000 to evaluate substance abuse treatment programs.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision that funds substance abuse and mental health programs and sets limits on how the amounts may be used. The tempting reading is that "Protection and Advocacy for Individuals with Mental Illness Act" or "national surveys on drug abuse" signals outside involvement, but the first is only a statute's name and the second is data collection, not consultation on a federal decision. Nothing in the section requires comment, hearings, advisory bodies, consultation with non-federal parties, or a right to sue.
fable.s: no funds appropriated for carrying out section 520A are available for carrying out section 1971 of the PHS Act

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that allocates specific dollar amounts for various federal programs and activities. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation by non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The text merely specifies funding levels and restrictions on how those funds can be used.
qwen_block.s: For carrying out titles V and XIX of the Public Health Service Act (“PHS Act”) with respect to substance abuse and mental health services, the Protection and Advocacy for Individuals with Mental Illness Act, and section 301 of the PHS Act with respect to program management, $3,237,813,000

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision. It sets funding amounts and percentage caps for substance abuse and mental health programs, and it sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The drug-abuse surveys collect data rather than consulting outsiders before a federal decision, and 'Protection and Advocacy' is only the name of a statute, so neither counts as participation.
opus.s: (3) $16,000,000 to carry out national surveys on drug abuse; and (4) $4,300,000 to evaluate substance abuse treatment programs.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that the funding for "national surveys on drug abuse" and the mention of the "Protection and Advocacy for Individuals with Mental Illness Act" bring outside people into federal decisions. That doesn't hold up. A national survey collects data from people; it doesn't consult them before a federal decision. "Protection and Advocacy" is just the name of a statute. The section only appropriates money and caps how much can go to certain activities.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation clause that allocates funds for specific agency activities such as technical assistance, data collection, and evaluation. It does not require consultation with, or participation by, outside parties in the decision-making process. The mention of surveys and evaluations refers to internal agency functions, not public participation mechanisms like hearings or advisory committees.
qwen_chat.s: For carrying out titles V and XIX of the Public Health Service Act (“PHS Act”) with respect to substance abuse and mental health services, the Protection and Advocacy for Individuals with Mental Illness Act, and section 301 of the PHS Act with respect to program management, $3,237,813,000
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "evaluation activities" and "national surveys," which might involve public input.
Resolution: These are internal agency activities (data collection, evaluation) funded by appropriations. There is no requirement for the public or outside entities to participate in the decision-making process; the text simply allocates money for the agency to conduct these activities.
